title: ojee.console — cockpit concept
question: The roll assigned the panoramic cockpit display. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Panoramic Cockpit Display
options.lineage: F-35 Lightning II single-panel glass cockpit
options.thesis: The console as one wide glass cockpit panel, every module a portal.
materials: vector stroke symbology on true black
portal bezels on one glass panel
options.viewport: Desktop: one landscape panel of portals around a spinnable 3D airframe of your network; phone: portals stack as pages behind soft-key tabs.
options.risk: Tips into movie-prop HUD if symbology decorates instead of measuring.

raised.raise: Fixed mask: instruments never reflow; only what is lit changes, and unlit cells are drawn as ghosts.
Colour is law: each cockpit colour means one state only; amber is caution, red is warning, never decoration.
Billing by severity: the system that needs you is drawn largest; healthy ones shrink to a line.
True black owns the panel: no grey fills or card backgrounds, only strokes and light.
Colour lives on instrument strokes; text stays white unless it carries a state.
One continuous panel: every portal arrangement is a recoverable, deep-linkable state.

options.label: Bezel-Button MFD
options.lineage: F-16 / F/A-18 multifunction displays with option-select buttons
options.thesis: Every module is a display page, picked by labelled buttons round the screen's edge.
options.viewport: Two square MFDs either side of a scratchpad clock; phone: one MFD, bezel buttons along the bottom edge.
options.risk: Where most cockpit-themed dashboards land, and square displays waste a wide screen.

options.label: Seven-Segment Panel
options.lineage: bedside clocks, price totems and scoreboards
options.thesis: Every number on the console is lit segments in a fixed mask; absence is drawn too.
options.viewport: The clock at full width in segment cells, module values in fixed cells beneath it.
options.case: Wins the watch-setting job; loses the fighter-cockpit identity and fits text facts badly.
options.risk: Module facts are sentences, not digits; drifts toward a petrol-station totem.

options.label: Arcade Cabinet CRT
options.thesis: The console as an arcade attract screen with phosphor glow.
options.viewport: Score-style readouts pinned to the top, modules as tiles on a pixel grid.
options.case: Loses both: reads as a game, not an instrument you trust.
options.kept: Palette law: each colour means exactly one state.

options.label: Festival Lineup Sheet
options.thesis: Hierarchy by type size alone; the headliner is what needs you.
options.viewport: Modules billed by urgency, largest first, as justified type.
options.case: Loses both: no instruments, and a saturated ground fights true black.
options.kept: Billing by severity: size says what matters.

options.label: Floating Capsules
options.thesis: Detached pill controls floating over one colour field.
options.viewport: A green field with white capsule nav and rounded panels.
options.case: Loses both: rounded and soft, the opposite of a cockpit.
options.kept: Total commitment of one ground: here, true black.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: Achromatic fields with colour only on hairline edges.
options.viewport: White field, grey text, pastel bands on the edges.
options.case: Loses both: a light, pastel world is the reverse of the brief.
options.kept: Colour lives on strokes; text stays achromatic.

options.label: Origami Fold Sequence
options.thesis: One uncut sheet passing through numbered, recoverable states.
options.viewport: A folding diagram with numbered steps in a margin column.
options.case: Loses both: paper craft has nothing to do with a cockpit.
options.kept: One continuous surface whose every state is recoverable.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A self-hosted dashboard as Home Assistant and Grafana ship it, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar, a grid of rounded status cards and small charts.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every self-hosted dashboard by design.
